title: Storage IaC safeguards: encryption-first EBS/EFS/S3 module with snapshot orchestration and passive health probes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Build a single, opinionated Terraform module used by Redwood Private that provisions and configures block, file, and object storage (EBS, EFS, S3) with secure defaults, automated snapshot lifecycle orchestration, and lightweight passive health probes for early detection of backup/restore and mount failures. Scope includes module APIs, KMS integration defaults, snapshot retention policies, cross-account snapshot sharing hooks for DR, and a small health-check Lambda to validate mounts and snapshot accessibility on a schedule. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, documentation, and an initial canary rollout for two existing customer VPCs.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes explicit inputs for encryption_kms_key_id, snapshot_retention_days, lifecycle_transition_policy, and enable_passive_healthcheck

All created EBS volumes, EFS file systems, and S3 buckets default to customer-managed KMS keys when provided and fall back to a secure KMS policy-managed key; no plaintext/unencrypted resources are created
Snapshot orchestration runs via a configurable AWS Backup plan or custom lifecycle (configurable per resource) and enforces snapshot_retention_days with automatic deletion of expired snapshots

Passive health-check Lambda (or Step Function) can be optionally attached to a VPC to validate: EBS snapshot restore smoke test, EFS mount+read/write probe, and S3 object round-trip; failures generate metrics and an alert to the console project topic
Module includes automated IAM least-privilege templates for cross-account snapshot sharing and clear docs on required roles/policies
Unit/integration Terraform test harness (Terratest or local-terraform plan validation) included and green in CI
Documentation in the infra repo and a short runbook for on-call describing common failures and remediation steps
Canary rollout executed to two internal VPCs; any issues logged and triaged before broader rollout
implementation_notes: Prefer a single module with resource wrappers: redwood_storage (type map) where type in {ebs, efs, s3} to reduce drift and encourage consistent defaults
Keep AWS Backup optional: some customers want native snapshot hooks. Provide an aws_backup_plan submodule and a fallback cron-driven Lambda snapshotter for air-gapped scenarios
KMS strategy: default to a module-managed KMS key with key rotation enabled and grant principal inputs for customer KMS if passed; ensure key policy disallows accidental deletion
Snapshot retention: implement lifecycle tag-based TTL and a controller Lambda that enforces deletion (safer than relying solely on provider retention settings when cross-account sharing is enabled)

Health checks: lightweight Lambda executed in-customer VPC via CloudWatch Events with an SNS alert path. Keep probes read-only where possible; EFS probe may write small sentinel file and delete it. EBS probe uses small restore into ephemeral volume and checks mount/read.
IaC testing: add Terratest suite to create a tiny EFS & S3 in a disposable account, run probes, confirm KMS encryption metadata, create a snapshot and validate TTL enforcement
Backward-compat: when upgrading existing stacks, module must detect existing unencrypted resources and fail-plan with clear remediation guidance (do not auto-convert without explicit consent)
Expect ~2 additional IAM roles and 1 new Lambda; keep costs minimal by tuning probe frequency to 6h by default
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): deploy module to two internal VPCs used by infra and SE teams with enable_passive_healthcheck=true and monitor for 7 days
Phase 2 (Pilot): invite two small customers for pilot migration guidance and docs feedback
Phase 3 (General): publish module in internal registry, announce in infra-eng, offer migration runbook and one-click Terraform snippet for Private deployments
Rollback: remove health-check schedule and revert to previous module version; snapshot lifecycle deletion is irreversible so plan removal carefully
qa_checks: Terraform plan must show no plaintext-creation diffs for KMS or storage resources
CI Terratest runs pass in disposable AWS account and assert encryption metadata
Health-check Lambda executes successfully in canary and records pass metric; any failed probe creates P0 alert to #infra-alerts
Manual restore smoke test documented and executed by assignee during rollout
